answer: Ledger-history cohort linking. Each identity’s transaction graph is embedded; clusters whose subgraphs are statistically indistinguishable from a common controller—shared counterparties, timing, sequence patterns—are flagged as one actor. Enforcement: flagged clusters earn as a single quota, not many. An attacker must generate genuinely distinct behavior per identity, like separating ivory from shale, costing sustained effort; merging them, even quartz-rare outliers, collapses the cohort.
